mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the negative median return is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4.0% in one month compared to previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered months compared to non-triggered months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative median return over triggered periods, or positive returns in more than 50% of triggered 60-day horizons.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals broad-based demand weakness, which amplifies recession risk and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative median return is not statistically significant at p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp cut in federal funds rates by more than 0.75 percentage points within a quarter signals an aggressive easing cycle, which lowers long-term yields and boosts risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher during triggered episodes, or positive returns occur in fewer than 55% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month is contradictory and signals a data anomaly or revision shock; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exhibit elevated volatility and are more likely to be negative.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: No significant increase in negative 5-day returns during triggered episodes, or the frequency of negative returns is not higher than baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 5-year average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and weaker consumption momentum, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: post-shock recovery or uncertainty-driven savings cycle
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods, or positive returns occur in more than 50% of triggered episodes.
